\section[scorso / scorsa]{scorso / scorsa — last (week, month, year)}

\label{lesson:IT-C137-scorso}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to find, then the Italian for to look for.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: scorso / scorsa}
\textbf{scorso / scorsa} — \textquotedblleft{}last (week, month, year)\textquotedblright{}. It follows the time word and agrees with it: \textbf{la settimana scorsa}, \textbf{il mese scorso}, \textbf{l'anno scorso}. With the passato prossimo: \textbf{La settimana scorsa ho lavorato.} — \textquotedblleft{}Last week I worked.\textquotedblright{}

\end{itemize}

\section[già]{già — already}

\label{lesson:IT-C137-gia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to look for, then the Italian for last.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: già}
\textbf{già} — \textquotedblleft{}already\textquotedblright{}. It sits between \textbf{ho} and the participle: \textbf{Ho già capito.} — \textquotedblleft{}I have already understood.\textquotedblright{} \textbf{Sono già tornato.} — \textquotedblleft{}I have already come back.\textquotedblright{}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{già}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for to look for, then the Italian for last, then say \emph{già} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does già mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Already\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[l'altro ieri]{l'altro ieri — the day before yesterday}

\label{lesson:IT-C137-laltro-ieri}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for last, then the Italian for already.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'altro ieri}
\textbf{l'altro ieri} — \textquotedblleft{}the day before yesterday\textquotedblright{}. One day further back than \textbf{ieri}: \textbf{L'altro ieri ho scritto una lettera.} — \textquotedblleft{}The day before yesterday I wrote a letter.\textquotedblright{}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for last, then the Italian for already, then say \emph{l'altro ieri} again

\section[recentemente]{recentemente — recently}

\label{lesson:IT-C137-recentemente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for already, then the Italian for the day before yesterday.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: recentemente}
\textbf{recentemente} — \textquotedblleft{}recently\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{Recentemente ho letto molto.} — \textquotedblleft{}Recently I have read a lot.\textquotedblright{} The ending \textbf{-mente} makes an adverb, the way English uses -ly.

\section[succedere]{succedere — to happen}

\label{lesson:IT-C137-succedere}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the day before yesterday, then the Italian for recently.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: succedere}
\textbf{succedere} — \textquotedblleft{}to happen\textquotedblright{}. Its past takes \textbf{essere}, like \textbf{andare}: \textbf{Che cosa è successo?} — \textquotedblleft{}What happened?\textquotedblright{}
